key_insight: HadBalance adds a unified, global shape prior for biomedical segmentation and uses gradient-aware balancing so the prior helps without overriding true anatomical details.
clinical_relevance: It may improve segmentation consistency across organs and imaging modalities, especially when boundaries are weak or shapes are noisy.
method: Derives Hadwiger shape priors from area, perimeter, and Euler characteristic as a global geometric regularizer.
Uses Conflict-Aware Objective Balancing to remove only prior-gradient components that conflict with segmentation gradients.
Adaptively controls objective strength to reduce over-regularization on heterogeneous anatomy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a plug-and-play framework designed for generalizable biomedical segmentation across organs and modalities, but it does not provide specific dataset sizes or quantitative results.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is that strong near-convex priors can still suppress genuine concavities or fine structures if balancing is not tuned carefully.
paper_title: HadBalance: A Plug-and-Play Unified Global Geometric Prior Framework for Generalizable Biomedical Segmentation
